text: Nebula, vast clouds of gas and dust in space, are the birthplaces of new stars. These intricate structures, often visible through telescopes, reveal the raw materials from which stars are constructed. As gravity forces this debris to collapse, the gravitational pressure creates a core known as a protostar, gradually heating the nebula. Over time, the young star may illuminate the nebula's dust, forming glowing patterns that reveal the star's formation process. Telescopes enhance our ability to explore these cosmic laboratories, providing closer insights into the dynamic evolution of starbirth regions.
